html:
"Pomerania" is the map's label, for 1000, for the Slavic peoples of the southern Baltic coast. The name comes from the Slavic po more, "by the sea". On the map the area sits around the lower Oder and to the west of it.

These West Slavs lived in strongholds and trading towns such as Wolin and Szczecin, where Slavic, Scandinavian and German merchants met. Around 1000 the Polish rulers Mieszko I and his son held part of the coast, and a bishopric was set up at Kołobrzeg at the Congress of Gniezno in 1000, but it soon collapsed and the Pomeranians stayed pagan.

In the 1120s Poland conquered them again, and Otto of Bamberg baptised them. A local family, the Griffins, ruled the Duchy of Pomerania, which later came under the Holy Roman Empire and slowly became German-speaking.
